hero.title: DeepSeek,
hero.lede: The High-Flyer-funded lab whose R1 release shook markets in January 2025. It speaks through model releases and papers, complies with Beijing on the day, and gives foreign regulators the minimum.

short_answer.title: Its releases are the trigger
short_answer.body: DeepSeek releases on its own cadence; others answer it. Baidu, Huawei and MIIT all moved within weeks of R1.

short_answer.title: Minimal answers abroad, same-day compliance at home
short_answer.body: Foreign bans get a jurisdiction denial or a market exit; China’s labelling measures got compliance on the day they took effect.

purpose.summary: What DeepSeek releases and how it answers regulators is in its control, so its record can forecast the behaviour of a frontier Chinese open-weight lab.
use_for: When a foreign government restricts DeepSeek, what does it do?
When Beijing pushes domestic chips, does DeepSeek align its models with Chinese hardware?
When a CAC rule takes effect, does DeepSeek comply on time?
dont_use_for: Release timing, which follows its own research schedule.
US chip smuggling claims, which DeepSeek does not answer.

standing.class_role: Company · private AI lab funded by the quant fund High-Flyer; MIT-licensed open weights.
standing.principal: Founder Liang Wenfeng and High-Flyer; no outside investors in this log.
standing.attribution_rule: A row is DeepSeek’s when it comes from the company: releases, API notices, papers, or Liang Wenfeng speaking for it.
standing.veto_players: CAC (filing and labelling), Beijing on chips, foreign data regulators (Italy, Korea, Berlin), US agencies.
standing.gates_held: Open weights: anyone can run its models, including Baidu Search and Huawei’s Ascend cloud.

powers.use: Frontier open-weight releases on its own cadence
powers.limit: R2 reportedly delayed by training on Ascend (DS14)
Funded by High-Flyer; no investments in this log
No formal partnerships in this log
No published safety framework found in this log
Silent on distillation and chip claims (DS22)

incentives: Research-driven pursuit of AGI, funded by High-Flyer and not dependent on revenue
Lower inference cost so APIs are cheap enough for everyone, priced at cost
Credibility with the Chinese state (Li Qiang and Xi symposia) and the domestic-chip ecosystem
Global developer adoption through MIT-licensed weights
red_lines: No public engagement with US or EU political criticism (bans, distillation, H100 claims)
Speaks only via official channels ('Please rely only on our official accounts')
Will not publicly contradict Chinese regulators; complies on effective dates
profile.decision_style: Quiet and engineering-led. Founder Liang rarely speaks and leaves no on-record statements after 2024 interviews. Releases are terse posts on api-docs, Hugging Face and GitHub, often right before holidays. Acts are technical (weights, kernels, papers) rather than rhetorical. It reacts to foreign pressure by doing little or withdrawing rather than arguing.

positions.position: Aligns with Chinese hardware when Beijing pushes domestic chips

relations.note: Complies with CAC rules on the effective date
R1 set off Baidu’s open-source reversal

voice.summary: Terse, technical posts on official channels; the founder rarely speaks.

say_do.do: Announces a significant price increase in August 2026

incidents.what_changed: Denied operating in Italy; app removed from Italian stores

incidents.incident: Anthropic accuses DeepSeek of industrial-scale distillation

rules.name: Foreign restriction → minimal response
rules.then: DeepSeek gives a minimal answer sized to the market: a jurisdiction denial, a market exit or silence, the same day
rules.note: One clean episode (Italy). DS09 says the app was pulled after the Garante’s questions, which may predate the formal block. The Korea suspension took effect before the regulator announced it; the Berlin case drew silence, logged but not counted.

rules.name: NVIDIA access cut → align with Chinese chips
rules.when: Beijing or Washington cuts NVIDIA supply in China
rules.then: DeepSeek aligns its next release with Chinese hardware (FP8 formats, Ascend support) within weeks to months
rules.note: The V4 release with Huawei day-0 support (DS24) falls after the cutoff.

rules.name: CAC rule takes effect → same-day compliance
rules.then: DeepSeek posts a terse compliance notice on the effective date

episodes.label: Outbound PI certification measures take effect (CAC O20), no DeepSeek notice

limits.title: Little on the record
limits.body: The founder has made almost no on-record statements since 2024; several quotes come from translations.

limits.title: Single-source rows
limits.body: DS25 (price increase) rests on one 36Kr article; DS24 is dated to the month.

limits.title: One coder
limits.body: Triggers were coded once (P6 not done).
